rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One explanation says the verse was revealed to answer idolaters who challenged the claim that their God is one after hearing 2:163.
rows.anchor: أنزلها عليه احتجاجا له على أهل الشرك به من عبدة الأوثان

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ataa reports that Quraysh asked how one God could suffice for everyone after 2:163, so this verse was sent to show He is God and creator of all.
rows.anchor: عن عطاء، قال " نزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالمدينة

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another explanation says polytheists asked Muhammad for a sign, and the created order itself supplies clear evidence of God's oneness to anyone who reasons.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل نزلت هذه الآية على النبي

rows.speaker: أبو الضحى
rows.claim: Abu al-Duha reports that after 2:163 the polytheists demanded a sign, prompting revelation of 2:164.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الضحى، قال " لما نزلت {وإلهكم إله واحد

rows.speaker: أبو الضحى
rows.claim: In another report, the polytheists marveled at the declaration of one God and demanded proof if Muhammad was truthful.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الضحى، قال " لما نزلت هذه الآية جعل المشركون

rows.speaker: عطاء بن أبى رباح
rows.claim: Ataa ibn Abi Rabah reports that the polytheists asked the Prophet to show them a sign, and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن عطاء بن أبى رباح: أن المشركين، قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: سعيد
rows.claim: Sa'id recounts Quraysh asking Jews and Christians about Moses's and Jesus's miracles, then asking for al-Safa to become gold; the Prophet sought respite, and the verse points to creation as a greater sign.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد، قال " سألت قريش، اليهود، فقالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation means originating and bringing the heavens and earth into existence after they did not exist; al-Tabari says he has already explained why “earth” is singular.
rows.anchor: إن في إنشاء السموات والأرض وابتداعهما

rows.speaker: بعض الناس
rows.claim: One theological view treats a thing's creation as something other than the thing, reasoning that God's will is a created thing through which other things exist.
rows.anchor: فقال بعض الناس: لها خلق هو غيرها

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: A second view says creation is an attribute of a thing, neither identical with it nor separate from it; making it separate would entail an endless regress of created attributes.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: خلق الشيء صفة له، لا هي هو ولا غيره.

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: A third view identifies a thing's creation with the thing itself, so “in the creation of the heavens and earth” means in the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: خلق السموات والأرض وخلق كل مخلوق، هو ذلك الشيء بعينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night and day differ by succeeding one another: when one departs, the other takes its place, as 25:62 also says.
rows.anchor: كل واحد منهما يخلف مكان صاحبه إذا ذهب الليل جاء النهار بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zuhayr's verse uses khalfa for things that alternate or follow one another, illustrating the meaning of “ikhtilaf.”
rows.anchor: من خلوف كل واحد منهما الآخر، كما قال تعالى ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Layl is the plural of layla, and layali adds a yāʾ in the plural as do forms such as rubāʿiyya, thamāniya, and karāhiyya.
rows.anchor: وأما الليل فإنه جمع ليلة، نظير التمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs rarely pluralize nahār because it is like light, though nahr is attested; a poet uses it, and anhar would be a regular diminutive plural.
rows.anchor: وأما النهار فإن العرب لا تكاد تجمعه لأنه بمنزلة الضوء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-fulk means ships; one form serves for singular and plural and may be masculine or feminine. The feminine allati suits ships set in motion and thus running.
rows.anchor: وهي مجراة؛ لأنها إذا أجريت فهي الجارية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ships benefit people at sea.
rows.anchor: فإن معناه: ينفع الناس في البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water sent from heaven is rain; reviving the dead earth means restoring it, making it flourish, and bringing forth vegetation. “Death” means ruined, barren ground with its provision-producing growth cut off.
rows.anchor: وموت الأرض: خرابها ودثور عمارتها، وانقطاع نباتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Batha means to disperse, as when a ruler sends troops out; dabba is an active participle from dabba, “to move,” and names living creatures other than winged birds because they move on the earth.
rows.anchor: والدابة الفاعلة من قول القائل دبت الدابة تدب دبيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grammar suppresses the agent and attaches the verbal noun to its object; God directs winds by sending them as pollinators, making them barren, or sending them as destructive punishment.
rows.anchor: ويبعثها عذابا تدمر كل شيء بأمر ربها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says God can make winds a sterile, nonpollinating punishment for those against whom they are sent.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وتصريف الرياح والسحاب المسخر}

rows.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
rows.claim: Some grammarians interpret this as winds coming from different directions, but al-Tabari says that describes their variation, not God's directing them; he allows the sense of God's directing their different courses.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعض أهل العربية أن معنى قوله: {وتصريف الرياح}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clouds is a collective noun from cloud, whose adjective appears masculine singular as with “date” and “palm”; its name likely describes clouds pulling one another, from the verb for dragging. 13:12 likewise uses the collective.
rows.anchor: وإنما قيل للسحاب سحاب إن شاء الله لجر بعضه بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are signs and proofs that the creator and originator of all things is one God; people of reason understand the evidence for His oneness.
rows.anchor: فإنه علامات ودلالات على أن خالق ذلك كله ومنشئه إله واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God directs proofs to rational, discerning people because they alone are addressed by commands and prohibitions and held accountable for worship, reward, and punishment.
rows.anchor: فأعلم تعالى ذكره عباده بأن الأدلة، والحجج إنما وضعت معتبرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument addresses polytheists who already acknowledge God as creator but worship idols alongside Him; their denial does not erase the signs of a creator and incomparable governor.
rows.anchor: بأن الله خالقهم غير أنهم يشركون في عبادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs enumerate God's exclusive blessings: sun and moon sustain livelihood, rain restores land, livestock provide food and clothing, and winds and clouds support crops, people, and herds; 30:40 challenges whether partners can do this.
rows.anchor: فأخبرهم أن إلههم هو الله الذي أنعم عليهم بهذه النعم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse addresses people who acknowledge God as creator yet associate partners, rather than atheists and materialists; even the smallest sign could persuade all people, but al-Tabari omits further detail to avoid length.
rows.anchor: هم القوم الذين وصفت صفتهم دون المعطلة، والدهرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahilla means “made lawful” or “permitted,” laylat al-siyam means during the night of fasting, and rafath is a euphemism here for intercourse; al-Tabari also mentions Abdullah's recitation. Elsewhere rafath can mean obscene speech.
rows.anchor: والرفث في غير هذا الموضع الإفحاش في المنطق كما قال العجاج

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains rafath as intercourse, saying God is gracious and speaks euphemistically.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: الرفث: الجماع، ولكن الله كريم يكني

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas glosses rafath as sexual relations.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال " الرفث: النكاح

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses rafath as approaching or having intercourse with women.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قال " الرفث: غشيان النساء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses rafath as intercourse.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله " {أحل لكم ليلة الصيام

rows.speaker: سالم بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Salim ibn Abdullah likewise says rafath means intercourse.
rows.anchor: سالم بن عبد الله عن قوله

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says rafath here means intercourse.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، {أحل لكم ليلة الصيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of spouses being garments is bodily closeness: each covers the other in bed, like clothing on the body; the poem of Nabigha ibn Ja'da illustrates the image.
rows.anchor: إذا ما الضجيع ثنى عطفها

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabi glosses each spouse as a cover or quilt for the other.
rows.anchor: عن الربيع {هن لباس لكم وأنتم لباس لهن}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation is that each spouse is the other's tranquility and place of repose, as night is called clothing in 25:47 and a spouse is made so one may dwell with her in 7:189.
rows.anchor: والوجه الآخر أن يكون جعل كل واحد منهما لصاحبه لباسا لأنه سكن له،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says spouses are a place of rest and tranquility for each other.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، {هن لباس لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possible sense is that each spouse conceals the other's sexual intimacy from other people's sight.
rows.anchor: فجائز أن يكون قيل: هن لباس لكم، وأنتم لباس لهن،

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi explains the garment image as spouses being tranquility for each other.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، " {هن لباس لكم}

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd interprets the image as sexual intercourse.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الرحمن بن زيد، في قوله " {هن لباس لكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says each spouse is the other's tranquility.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {هن لباس لكم وأنتم لباس لهن}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The self-betrayal comprised two things: sexual relations with wives and eating or drinking during the period when those acts were forbidden.
rows.anchor: ذكرها الله في شيئين: أحدهما جماع النساء، والآخر: المطعم

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Layla reports the earlier rule: after sleeping before the evening meal, fasting people could neither eat nor have relations; reports about Umar and an Ansari led to this permission.
rows.anchor: ثنا ابن أبي ليلى، " أن الرجل كان إذا أفطر فنام

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى
rows.claim: In another account, the elderly Ansari Sirma slept before eating and woke to continue fasting; Umar also had relations after his wife slept, and the verse lifted both hardships.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى، قال " كانوا يصومون ثلاثة أيام من كل شهر

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: Muadh reports that people stopped eating, drinking, and having relations after sleep; Abu Sirma became exhausted after labor, while another man violated the rule concerning women, and the verse followed.
rows.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل، قال " كانوا يأكلون ويشربون ويأتون النساء

rows.speaker: البراء
rows.claim: Al-Bara recounts an Ansari who worked, fell asleep before iftar, and awoke exhausted; the permission to eat and drink until dawn was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن البراء، نحو حديث ابن أبي ليلى

rows.speaker: البراء
rows.claim: A second al-Bara report names Qays ibn Sirma: after work he slept before eating, became severely hungry, and the verse allowing night relations and food was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن البراء، قال " كان أصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا كان الرجل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says early Muslims could eat only until the evening prayer and then had to fast through sleep until the next night; some, including Umar, broke the rules, so the verse permitted relations, food, and drink until dawn.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قول الله تعالى ذكره {أحل لكم ليلة الصيام

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Ka'b ibn Malik reports that after his wife slept Umar had intercourse with her, and Ka'b did likewise; Umar told the Prophet, after which this permission was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه، قال " كان الناس في رمضان إذا صام الرجل فأمسى فنام

rows.speaker: ثابت
rows.claim: Thabit reports that Umar had intercourse with his wife on a Ramadan night and felt distressed, so the permission was revealed.
rows.anchor: ثنا ثابت، " أن عمر بن الخطاب، واقع، أهله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts Umar's remorse after intercourse under the old rule; God then revealed forgiveness and allowed intercourse, food, and drink until dawn.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله " {أحل لكم ليلة الصيام الرفث}

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says earlier a person who slept after sunset could neither eat, drink, nor have relations until the next night; those who broke the rule were forgiven and allowed these acts throughout the night.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، {أحل لكم ليلة الصيام الرفث إلى نسائكم}

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima reports that an unnamed Ansari fell asleep while his wife prepared food, then became faint while fasting; the dispensation was revealed for him.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، مولى ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada describes the early fast as three days each month and then Ramadan: eating, drinking, and sex became forbidden after sleep, but the verse allowed all three until dawn.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة: {علم الله أنكم كنتم تختانون أنفسكم}

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says anyone who slept after nightfall had previously been barred from food, drink, and sex until the following night; violations prompted God's concession.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {أحل لكم ليلة الصيام الرفث إلى نسائكم}

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the Christians' Ramadan rule against eating, drinking, or sex after sleep had been imposed on Muslims; after Abu Qays became exhausted and Umar and others confessed to intercourse, the verse permitted these acts until dawn.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، قال " كتب على النصارى رمضان، وكتب عليهم أن لا يأكلوا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi glosses self-betrayal as intercourse with wives and “then have relations” as sexual intercourse.
rows.anchor: يقول: إنكم تقعون عليهن خيانة

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ataa says the earlier rule barred food, drink, and sex after sleeping; an Ansari who had relations after sleep said he had betrayed himself, and revelation allowed all three until dawn.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: قلت لعطاء {أحل لكم ليلة الصيام

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid repeats that people who slept after sunset had violated the ban on sex, food, and drink, which was then lifted for the entire night.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد، " كان أصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم يصوم الصائم

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima relates Umar having relations after his wife slept and says the eat-and-drink permission concerned Abu Qays ibn Sirma, who ate after sleeping.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، أنه قال في هذه الآية: {أحل لكم ليلة الصيام

rows.speaker: محمد بن يحيى بن حبان
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban reports that the elderly Sirma ibn Anas fell asleep before eating after fasting and work, so the permission to eat and drink until dawn was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن يحيى بن حبان، " أن صرمة بن أنس، أتى أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic mubashara literally means skin touching skin; here it euphemistically means intercourse, permitted on Ramadan nights until dawn.
rows.anchor: فأما المباشرة في كلام العرب: فإنه ملاقاة بشرة ببشرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains mubashara as intercourse, with God graciously using a euphemism.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال " المباشرة: الجماع، ولكن الله كريم يكني

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another Ibn Abbas gloss translates “now have relations” as “marry them.”
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A further Ibn Abbas report glosses mubashara as sexual relations.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال " المباشرة: النكاح

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ataa says mubashara means intercourse, and that every Qur'anic occurrence of mubashara means the act of intercourse itself; Abd Allah ibn Kathir is reported to agree.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: قلت لعطاء، قوله {فالآن باشروهن}

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report through Sa'id ibn Jubayr, says mubashara means intercourse, though God may use whichever euphemism He wills.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، قال «المباشرة الجماع

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi glosses the command to have relations as “have intercourse with them.”
rows.anchor: عن السدي، " {فالآن باشروهن}

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and Ataa both gloss mubashara in the Book as intercourse.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال المباشرة: الجماع

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says “seek what God ordained for you” means seek offspring; reports also attribute this interpretation to al-Hakam, Ikrima, al-Hasan, al-Suddi, Ibn Abbas, and al-Rabi.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، {وابتغوا ما كتب الله لكم}

rows.speaker: الأوزاعي
rows.claim: Al-Awzai reports Mujahid's view that mubashara in the Qur'an means intercourse.
rows.anchor: قال الأوزاعي: ثنا من سمع، مجاهدا يقول المباشرة في كتاب الله

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says “seek what God ordained” means sexual intercourse.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله " {وابتغوا ما كتب الله لكم}

rows.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim says it means offspring.
rows.anchor: سمعت الضحاك بن مزاحم، قوله " {وابتغوا ما كتب الله لكم}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through Abu al-Jawza interprets what was ordained as Laylat al-Qadr.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الجوزاء، عن ابن عباس، " {وابتغوا ما كتب الله لكم}

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets the phrase as pursuing what God made lawful and the concession He granted; he also reports a reading with “follow” instead of “seek.”
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، " {وابتغوا ما كتب الله لكم}

rows.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
rows.claim: Ataa asked Ibn Abbas whether to read “seek” or “follow”; Ibn Abbas accepted either but advised keeping the first reading.
rows.anchor: عن عطاء بن أبي رباح، قال: قلت لابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says the wording broadly means seek what God decreed and made available, including offspring, Laylat al-Qadr, or lawful things; offspring best fits the context of intercourse and has the clearest surface support.
rows.anchor: والصواب من القول في تأويل ذلك عندي أن يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation identifies the white thread as daylight and the black thread as night's darkness: eating, drinking, and intercourse may continue until dawn light emerges.
rows.anchor: فتأويله على قول قائل هذه المقالة: وكلوا بالليل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan glosses the white and black threads as night and day.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن، في قول الله تعالى ذكره

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the early false dawn should not end the pre-dawn meal: wait for the unmistakable dawn spreading horizontally across the horizon.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وكلوا واشربوا حتى يتبين لكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the white and black threads mean day and night; when dawn becomes clear, food, drink, and intercourse stop, and the fast continues until night.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {وكلوا واشربوا حتى يتبين لكم

rows.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
rows.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash rebukes a literal reading as night's departure and day's arrival; Adi reports the Prophet's clarification that the threads mean daylight and night.
rows.anchor: عن عدي بن حاتم، قال: قلت يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: سهل بن سعد
rows.claim: Sahl ibn Sa'd says the original wording lacked “from dawn”; some men tied black and white threads to their legs until God added the phrase to clarify that the threads mean night and day.
rows.anchor: عن سهل بن سعد، قال: نزلت هذه الآية:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True dawn is a diffuse whiteness spreading through the sky and lighting roads, unlike the vertical, bright false dawn.
rows.anchor: صفة ذلك البياض أن يكون منتشرا مستفيضا في السماء

rows.speaker: أبو مجلز
rows.claim: Abu Majliz says the bright streak in the sky is false dawn; true dawn appears when the horizon opens and becomes clear.
rows.anchor: عن أبي مجلز، «الضوء الساطع في السماء ليس بالصبح

rows.speaker: مسلم
rows.claim: Muslim says people did not count the dawn as true until it filled homes and roads.
rows.anchor: عن مسلم، قال «لم يكونوا يعدون الفجر فجركم هذا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas distinguishes two dawns: the one rising in the sky changes no ruling, but dawn visible over the mountain tops prohibits drinking.
rows.anchor: سمع ابن عباس، يقول «هما فجران، فأما الذي يسطع في السماء

rows.speaker: محمد بن عبد الرحمن بن ثوبان
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Thawban says the wolf-tail-like dawn prohibits nothing; the spread dawn across the horizon permits prayer and prohibits fasting.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن عبد الرحمن بن ثوبان

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: The Prophet says neither Bilal's call nor the elongated false dawn should stop the pre-dawn meal; only the dawn spread across the horizon does so.
rows.anchor: عن سمرة بن جندب، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: In another report, the Prophet says not to be deceived by Bilal's call or the early whiteness until dawn appears and breaks open.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه سمعه

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation takes the white thread to mean sunlight and the black thread to mean night.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: الخيط الأبيض: هو ضوء الشمس

rows.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Taymi recounts Hudhayfa continuing to eat after the feared dawn had appeared and delaying prayer, supporting the view that day begins only at sunrise.
rows.anchor: عن إبراهيم التيمي، قال: " سافر أبي، مع حذيفة

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reportedly said after praying dawn prayer that this was when the white thread became distinct from the black.
rows.anchor: عن هبيرة، عن علي، أنه لما صلى الفجر

rows.speaker: البراء
rows.claim: Al-Bara reports eating a late pre-dawn meal with Ibn Masud, who urged him to drink even though he had already eaten; they then went out while people were praying.
rows.anchor: عن البراء، قال: " تسحرت في شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: عامر بن مطر
rows.claim: Amir ibn Matar says Ibn Masud shared leftover pre-dawn food with him, then they went to prayer after it had been called.
rows.anchor: عن عامر بن مطر، قال «أتيت عبد الله بن مسعود

rows.speaker: سالم مولى أبي حذيفة
rows.claim: Salim says Abu Bakr first gestured for him to stop eating, then looked toward dawn and finally asked for food and ate before praying.
rows.anchor: عن سالم، مولى أبي حذيفة قال، كنت أنا وأبو بكر

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Conflicting reports from Ibrahim place suhur by day, by night, or between the second call and the prayer's commencement.
rows.anchor: عن إبراهيم، قال «الوتر بالليل، والسحور بالنهار»

rows.speaker: حبان بن الحارث
rows.claim: Hibban reports that he ate suhur with Ali and then went out as the prayer was being established.
rows.anchor: عن عروة، عن حبان، قال: «تسحرنا مع علي

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali is reported to have prayed dawn and said this was when the white thread became distinct from the black.
rows.anchor: عن أبي السفر، قال " صلى علي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Those identifying dawn with sunrise argue that day begins at sunrise as it ends at sunset; starting it at dawn would imply it ends at twilight, contrary to consensus, and reports show the Prophet eating after dawn.
rows.anchor: قالوا: وأول النهار طلوع الشمس، كما أن آخره غروبها.

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: Hudhayfa says he ate suhur with the Prophet and describes the time as day although the sun had not risen.
rows.anchor: عن حذيفة، قال: قلت: تسحرت مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم؟

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: Another report says the Prophet ate while dawn was near and visible, but the sun had not yet risen.
rows.anchor: عن حذيفة، قال " كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يتسحر

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet reportedly told a person hearing the call with a vessel in hand to finish drinking; one version says the caller sounded when dawn had begun.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: Abu Umama reports that when prayer was called with a vessel in Umar's hand, the Prophet permitted him to drink.
rows.anchor: عن أبي أمامة، قال " أقيمت الصلاة والإناء في يد عمر

rows.speaker: بلال
rows.claim: Bilal reports that the Prophet drank when Bilal came to announce dawn prayer and then shared the vessel before they went to prayer.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مغفل، عن بلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the Prophet's explicit explanation that the white thread is daybreak and the black thread is night, which matches ordinary Arabic usage; reports of drinking before prayer do not prove drinking after dawn, since the prayer followed dawn and its call preceded it.
rows.anchor: وأولى التأويلين بالآية، التأويل الذي روي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari reads Hudhayfa's “it is dawn” as meaning close to dawn rather than literally after dawn; Arabic may call something by the name of what it resembles.
rows.anchor: ولكنه قال: هو الصبح. وذلك من قوله يحتمل أن يكون معناه

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd describes the white thread as the line beneath the night that uncovers it, and the black thread as what lies above it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد: {حتى يتبين لكم الخيط الأبيض من الخيط الأسود من الفجر}
